name: Isoko

span.note: The start of the timeline, not a founding date. The end is approximate.

summary.text: Isoko clans were led by their eldest man, the Okpako Ewo, who held office by age: when he died, the next most senior elder took his place. There are nineteen clans: Uzere, Ozoro, Erowha, Owhe, Iyede, Okpe, Emede, Igbide, Emevor, Ofagbe, Ellu, Oyede, Umeh, Irri, Aviara, Olomoro, Enwhe, Okpolo and Oleh. Close to the Urhobo in speech and custom, they and the Urhobo were lumped together by Europeans as “Sobo”, a name both rejected.

reviewNotes: Needs a written source for the date British rule reached this people.

end.text: Like the Urhobo, the Isoko came under the British vice-consulates of the Niger Coast Protectorate in the 1890s.
